title: Sounding Like Which AI? Machine-Style Overlap of arXiv Abstracts with Language Models of Different Vintages: code, data and paper
description:
Code, released data, results and paper (preprint, not peer reviewed) for a study of Machine-Style Overlap (MSO): the share of documents that a calibrated classifier on content-word-free style features judges at least as likely to be LLM output as pre-ChatGPT human writing. It measures MSO in arXiv abstracts from 2015 to 2026 against reference generators of different vintages, with Australian parliamentary speech and student essays as secondary genres.

How it was made: the study was carried out by an AI system (Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic, via Claude Code) under the author's direction. The AI system wrote the code, ran the analyses and drafted the paper; the author chose the topic and constraints and is responsible for the content. See paper/AI_DISCLOSURE.md.

Details in README.md and data/README.md.
